scope: Issue #143 phase 3: Pi native Handle completion/retry/terminal properties and Pi RPC transport chunking, correlation, cancellation, failure cleanup and request-bound properties. Test-only change (tests/property/native-harness.property.test.ts, tests/property/pi-rpc.property.test.ts, tests/fixtures/fake-pi-rpc.mjs, tests/property/check.ts and documentation); no production module changed. The `faults` array below lists the nine mutations that substantiate acceptance criterion C4. Six of them were added while answering review findings rather than being part of the original set: `rpc-delivers-response-for-unknown-id` and `rpc-decodes-latin1` are the direct evidence that the correlation and chunking legs they answer for are load-bearing; `handle-keeps-summary-after-empty-turn` is the direct evidence for the earlier `native-harness.property.test.ts` finding that the empty settled turn was reachable only through a generated draw; `handle-clears-summary-on-stop-path` is the evidence for the later finding that the stop paths kept only one of their two halves asserted; and `rpc-fails-without-clearing-pending-bounds` and `rpc-failure-does-not-release-its-process` are the evidence for the finding that the failure-mode property could not tell a cleaned wait or a released process from one that only looked settled. All six are recorded here rather than being left as claims in a reply.

faults.edit: the streaming decoder is constructed as `new StringDecoder('latin1')` instead of `'utf8'`
faults.effect: the assembly stops being encoding-aware, so a record carrying a multi-byte character decodes to mojibake; the property detects that the decoder must be UTF-8. This is deliberately not read as evidence that a chunk boundary fell inside a character: a latin1 decoder is stateless per byte, so it yields the same text whether the record arrives whole or split, and the mutation would be detected under the pre-fix coalescing fixture too. See the guide's fault section, which states the same limit.

samples.native-harness.property.test.ts: The Pi family declares { normal: 30, explore: 100 }. The file default is { normal: 30, explore: 1000 }, which the three earlier Harness families inherit — they pass no sampleBudget at all — so the Pi family is the only one in this file that overrides it. The sample owns an in-process double, so all 30 samples cost about 230 ms. Seven examples are mandatory — the six Pi terminal paths and the empty completed turn — so they run first and count towards the 30 rather than adding to it.
samples.pi-rpc.property.test.ts: { normal: 8, explore: 60 } for the chunking, correlation and cancellation properties, { normal: 12, explore: 60 } for the failure-mode property and { normal: 6, explore: 30 } for the request bound, because each sample spawns a real child process and pays its startup, handshake and exit — in the delivered tier that is most of the 6.47 s the 42 samples cost — and the timeout property additionally advances a virtual clock. The failure-mode tier is 12 because its eight declared modes are mandatory examples: eight of the twelve samples are those modes, and four are generated. The cancellation property spends one of its eight samples on a mandatory mixed kept-and-cancelled example, so "only the requested work" is exercised by every run instead of by a draw that could cancel all of its entries or none.
samples.sampleCountDecision: The RPC families first declared 10 normal samples and were reduced to 8 (6 for the timeout property) after the first sweep showed real subprocess startup dominating. The failure-mode family was then raised back to 12, because eight of its samples are now mandatory examples and the tier has to be at least that long for all of them to run: fast-check takes `numRuns` values from the front of a stream whose head is the example list, so a tier below the example count would silently truncate the list instead of the generated samples. Coverage of a declared mode is therefore structural rather than a per-run draw. The delivered tier runs 42 samples in 6.47 s of test bodies, about 154 ms each. Criterion 5 asks for mocks at large scale and few real-subprocess regressions, which is why only the transport family spawns a process and only at the IO tier.

cost.method: Whole property suite (pnpm test:properties -- --reporter=verbose) on the same checkout and machine, 6 alternating runs with the property directory replaced by the base-SHA version (baseline) and by the candidate version (candidate). Vitest startup included; package install excluded. The six pairs were captured in one uninterrupted window with the machine to itself, and both legs still move by several seconds between captures, which is why all six pairs are reported and why the gate is read from the paired medians. pairedDifferencesSeconds is the same-round (chronological) difference, candidate run i minus baseline run i, which is the comparison the alternation exists to make. Ranking the two lists separately pairs them the same way in this sweep: 7.74 / 6.45 / 5.90 / 6.18 / 6.50 / 6.53. The swept candidate is identified by the propertySha256 entries above, which are the delivered revision of those files.

chunkBoundarySeparation.method: A probe spawns the same fixture over the same kind of pipe, drives a one-byte chunk plan with a boundary inside a three-byte character, and counts the reads that begin with a UTF-8 continuation byte. Such a read is proof that the previous read ended inside a character. The probe's reader is a plain pipe reader, not `rpc.ts`'s own, which a test-only change cannot instrument.
chunkBoundarySeparation.note: The pre-fix run without one issued 184 reads and none began with a continuation byte, so it reassembled every character inside a single read.
chunkBoundarySeparation.whyScoped: Yielding a timer at every interior boundary instead costs about 2 ms per boundary, which took the chunk-assembly property from about 1.3 s to about 4.3 s. In the sweep window that first tried it the candidate leg was 66.92 s against a 53.54 s baseline -- +13.38 s, over the ≤10 s gate -- which is why the guarantee is scoped rather than extended. That variant was measured and discarded. The kept artifact, every-boundary-yield-candidate.log, carries the candidate leg only; the baseline and the paired difference are recorded in .agents/local/151-evidence/finding-round7-fixes.txt.
